reviews.title: Actually Horrible
reviews.text: Don’t read any of these reviews. This app is completely pay to experience and hosting is a nightmare. There are queues for raiding and hosting because they push the premium queues so much. Using this app to what it should be like for everyone is just more of a paywall than Pokémon go already is. If you’re hardcore about raiding and willing to shell out a ton of money for it go ahead but the design of this app makes you believe as of they want you to have the best experience but their queue system has to be the worst algorithm I have ever experienced. The only way to interact with this app is to have remote raid passes already and find a pokémon you want but if you’re at all trying to engage with the app beyond surface level it will disappoint you to no end. If the developers were more transparent about their queue system or give hosts more control over their own lobbies this would immediately resolve all the issues that the algorithm creates. However it seems that it is intentional design to frustrate you and get you to spend on the premium features. The developers are beyond greedy to not only leech off the popularity and desire for remote raids and are using it as a cash grab for anyone simply interacting with this app. Again if the host had more control over their lobbies all of my criticism is mutt but it is unlikely to change because if it’s already making them money they have no reason to change the app.

reviews.title: So Unfair
reviews.text: I was really excited to use this app but the experience was ruined by an incredibly frustrating policy. I was temporarily banned simply because my Pokémon GO account isn’t a high enough level. Seriously? Instead of helping players improve and grow, the app punishes them for not already being at an arbitrary level. If someone is too low level for certain features, explain it restrict that specific feature if necessary or offer guidance. A 24 hour ban is completely over the top and makes absolutely no sense. It feels like you’re being punished for trying to use the app as intended. The app itself has some useful features but policies like this drive people away. Newer and returning players shouldn’t be treated like they’re doing something wrong just because they haven’t reached a certain level yet. Very disappointing experience and unless this policy changes, I can’t recommend this app.

reviews.title: Do not purchase anything in this app but free features work well
reviews.text:
TLDR: I have had a ton of success using reddit, discord and facebook, all of which were free, but this app is basically unusable for higher demand raids and paying to access “limited availability” raids is a complete and total waste of money. Borderline scam. 

The free features on this app are reliable and do what they are supposed to do. I frequently use this app for raids with Pokémon who are in low demand and it has worked great. Recently, mewtwo primal/shadow groudon/kyogre raids were happening for a limited time. The app pay walled the raids so I bought the cheapest (still insanely expansive) subscription. That was a huge mistake. Wait times have been 5+ hours at any given time for kyogre/groudon. Mewtwo queue is longer than a week at this point. I have only gotten one successful kyogre raid through this app after 3 days. I have had a ton of success using reddit, discord and facebook, all of which were free, but this app is basically unusable for higher demand raids and paying to access “limited availability” raids is a complete and total waste of money, borderline scam.

reviews.title: Great for solo, Mediocre for raids
reviews.text:
This app is great for the solo trainer. The IV calculator, name generator, and Pokedex all make this a wonderful tool for most of the game’s content. 

Where it fails, and fails hard, is raids, specifically high tier Dynamax raids. The app doesn’t allow players under a certain level to join these raids, but app users can very, very easily adjust their level to lie to get in. The game has the ability to scan and read screenshots, yet doesn’t require players to use a screenshot of their character or the Dynamax pokemon they intend to use, in order to prove they are capable of achieving the goal. So what you end up with is a team of 4 players, and if one of them isn’t a high enough level and/or doesn’t have good pokemon, the other players will all end up wasting a remote raid pass, which costs them real money or time and effort. And the game’s reporting feature clearly does next to nothing. Players that get too many negative reviews are banned from raiding for 10-15 minutes, but the they can go right back to raiding afterwards. If they get banned again, it’s only for another 10-15 minutes. There doesn’t seem to be any longer ban periods. Dynamax raids are not worth participating in through this app. You will end up wasting your own time, effort, sanity and money more often than winning, or even completing the raid.

reviews.title: Raid issues
reviews.text:
Downloaded this app as an alternative to the Niantic Campfire through Pokemon Go, which has its own issues with joining and hosting raids remotely. 
Poke Genie is a lot more user-friendly where you can specify which raid you want to join, unlike Campfire where you keep having to search until you come across one that you fancy. 
However, I recently spent 4 days waiting in a queue to join a combat Tauros raid, and when I finally got into a raid it was a blaze Tauros. So annoying. Spent another 4 days in a queue and finally joined a raid group only to not be sent a raid invite in the allotted time. Rather than let me re-join the queue as a priority, I’m now faced with being over 28,000 in the queue and another 5 or 6 day wait. This app needs to improve.

reviews.title: Bad for hosting raids
reviews.text: Pokegenie looks like a nice shiny way to get raids in from the outside and even has some pretty good features. But if you’re from the USA don’t download this app if you plan to Host remote raids. They’ve setup a pay to win system in which you go through a “first come first serve queue” in which 99% of the time you won’t make it through as a first time hoster. But queue times can  be improved by hosting more successful raids and getting higher ranked. Of course conveniently for pokegenie you can’t make it through a queue in time in order to actually host and get your rank up unless you plan to pay more than what you would on a remote raid pass for an hour long “boost”.  I definitely understand how a players continuous reliable support should be rewarded but first timers will continue to get buried by the queue times and never make it up through any ranks unless they waste more money on a singular raid than they would on a remote raid pass. Needless to say that’s the last time I waste an hour of my time on here trying to host a raid that will expire before I get through the queue when there’s truely FTP options available with more reliable outcomes.
